title: Term 3 and 4 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 3 and 4.

questions.prompt: In which city was the conference held in 1884–1885 to divide Africa?

questions.memo:

sections.title: QUESTION 3: The Causes of World War I
sections.instructions: Read the text below, then answer the questions.

context.title: Source D: The 'blank cheque' (a paraphrase of Germany's assurance to Austria-Hungary, July 1914)
context.text: Austria-Hungary must deal with Serbia firmly, and Germany will stand by her side as a faithful ally, whatever the consequences.

questions.prompt: In which years was World War I fought? (e.g. 1900–1905)
Who assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand?
In which city was Franz Ferdinand killed?

Match each cause to an example.

pairs.right: Europe divided into two armed camps
Serbs wanting a united Slav state

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a long-term cause and an immediate cause? Use World War I as an example.
questions.memo:
✓ Long-term causes build tension over many years, e.g. militarism, alliances, imperialism, nationalism (1)
✓ The immediate cause is the event that triggers the war: the assassination at Sarajevo (1)

questions.prompt: Read Source D. What promise is the Kaiser making, and why was it important?
questions.memo:
✓ Germany will support Austria-Hungary in whatever action it takes against Serbia (the 'blank cheque') (1)
✓ It encouraged Austria-Hungary to act aggressively, making war more likely (1)
